analysis: The closest option combines economics, public policy, economic behaviour and market organisation with research, calculus, probability, numerical modelling and econometrics. Numerical methods supports model approximation and replaces the business AI applications course only in this option. Behavioural Economics remains substantive, with psychology and deviations from standard models, and its selected fall term follows introductory microeconomics. International Business & Governance adds trade theory and policy. Money, Banking & Finance offers a stronger counterpart to Economics of Banking than the investment course. The business option builds from venture and product foundations to strategy, leadership, law, marketing and finance, with accounting, market research and quantitative tools. Consumer Product Design is moved to its first-year offering. The international and sustainability option adds environmental science, sustainability governance, climate communication, environmental justice and a renewable-system design project to economics, trade and financial context. Earth Observation replaces an advanced sustainability project only available in the first term, supplying geospatial methods after Sustainability Essentials I and introductory data analysis. Description-only Behavioural Economics, Econometrics, Market Research, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Social Movements & Environmental Justice and Renewable System Design contribute the actual subject and methods supported by their descriptions. The formal microeconomics course aligns with UCR microeconomics rather than negotiation. Dutch economy, advanced dynamic macroeconomics, labour economics, economic thought, the minor and the required economics thesis remain distinct. The three examples each exceed the pairwise course difference floor and address the three evidenced degree profiles, with minors informing focus within those alternatives.
